i was walking around a park chatting to a friend the other day

she mentioned her housemate can tell if someone is a good or bad person within three seconds

my friend wanted to learn how to do the same thing. this led to a discussion on intuition. i think it’s something that can be trained. mine has always been good but it’s grown stronger lately. it was always there but i didn’t always listen to it

my friend said her intuition is poor and she’d like to improve it. i noticed she didn’t make much eye contact. for me, eye contact is everything. i notice it too much. when i was younger, i had trouble holding it, sometimes too long, sometimes too short, so i learned what to do. now it feels natural. i hold it the right amount of time, most of the time. and i notice when others don’t. when the stare is too brief or too intense. longing, lust, contempt, curiosity. the eyes say so much. sometimes i wish i couldn’t read them so well

we later find out the housemate actually needs three sentences, not three seconds. that made more sense. i think i need more than three sentences. maybe a couple of minutes of conversation. not to tell if someone’s good or bad, just whether i like them. whether we’ll get on. what kinda mood they are in, etc. i've been wrong but i'm mostly right

a flood of info comes in through the eyes. some useful, some not. but it’s all info. and maybe some of it’s wrong sure but to discount it all feels so viscerally wrong. i hope i keep listening to my body. to my gut. the home of intuition

---

my new housemate is quite unusual. we only talk when we go grocery shopping and it's clear she doesn't actually need the groceries. we only go grocery shopping together since she was complaining how far away the supermarket is and heavy the bags are. we have been twice now and every time she buys some fruit and maybe a salad. they aren't heavy at all. i still help her carry them tho

she's clearly from a wealthy family. she doesn't cook and eats out every meal. she tells me she has visited many countries, she tells me to name a country and she’s probably been there. i ask her what she does for a living but she says she doesn't work. i wonder what she does all day. she can't be just visiting friends all day. that's what she says when i ask what have you been up to, "visiting friends". i wonder what else she does

she finds it funny i do so much tai chi and that i can cook. i tell her i can cook but i'm not that amazing at it. you pick it up the more you do it. i try to convince her to try but she doesn't seem like she wants to. i tell her my tai chi class has space if she's interested. she said she'll think about it. i already know she won't come but it’s nice to offer. i'm thinking about obsession now. i think i'm a lil obsessed

---

i did tai chi for 18 hours this week and thought about it for 18 hours more. i am chill about it to people tho. i don't bring it up every chance i get. i just tell them i do a bit of tai chi

i teach my first class tomorrow. a real class in a real classroom. i somehow managed to wrangle 4 friends to come. i hope they enjoy it. i hope i can teach one of them the whole short form. it'll take a couple of months of trying and that's only if they like doing it. one is enough i tell myself. i have a feeling one of them will stick with it. i wonder which one it will be...

i have an older gentleman in his 70s that requested tai chi lessons. twice a week. he had a fall recently and has lost his balance and confidence. the goal is to get him going back to classes in the main branch i go to. he used to go all the time but is afraid of falling again. he is a bit far away but i took the request as soon as it was mentioned. we need to call and arrange a meetup. i will find out more info next week. i would be very happy if we reach his goal. it will be my goal too. i'm getting ahead of myself tho. let's see if we get on during our first meeting. i hope we do and we can have some wonderful lessons together!
